title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a supply-chain manipulation aimed at large language models and AI-powered search systems. The method was not to attack the models directly but to inject fabricated authoritative content into the sources those models draw on. By producing a high volume of academically styled reports in a short period, through a platform explicitly designed to optimize content for chatbot citation, the operation attempted to shape what AI systems would present as established fact on contested geopolitical topics.

The failure mode this exposes sits upstream of the model itself. AI systems that retrieve or train on web content have no reliable way to verify the institutional legitimacy of a source, only its surface signals: citation patterns, formal prose, volume, and apparent consistency with other indexed material. A fake think tank that mimics those signals can pass through without triggering any check that a human editorial process might apply. Catching this would have required either robust provenance verification of sources before ingestion or active auditing of AI outputs for systematic framing patterns, neither of which is a standard feature of current deployment pipelines.

What is not established is whether the content was actually absorbed into any AI training dataset or materially altered any model's outputs, as the reporting describes the operation's intent and infrastructure rather than confirmed downstream effect.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli government-funded operation created a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to influence artificial intelligence systems toward pro-Israel messaging. The institute published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words in just nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for chatbot citations. The reports, presented in academic style with citations from legitimate sources, addressed contentious topics like Palestinian expulsions and genocide allegations while consistently framing information to minimize criticism of Israel.

The operation is part of a broader campaign financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through advertising company Havas Media to prime chatbots to make pro-Israel arguments. Researchers found the Hanover Institute was built on infrastructure designed for generative engine optimization, with plans to have its content absorbed into AI training datasets where it could influence chatbot responses without visible sourcing. The campaign represents a new strategy for foreign governments to manipulate artificial intelligence systems, raising broader concerns about information integrity in AI-generated content.
